The test embeds setup inline with hard-coded magic values (2450, -1582) and does not extract helper methods or constants. Although only one test exists (so duplication isn't visible), there is no modularization to support reuse or reduce duplication.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short, linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals. It follows a clear Given-When-Then structure and stays within reasonable line-count limits.

The test includes multiple meaningful assertions that verify different properties (vertex counts for both graphs and instance inequality). It checks several aspects of the transpose operation rather than a single superficial property.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the visible code. The test is active and contains up-to-date assertions and comments.
Class-level Javadoc includes a requirement ID (REQ-GRAFO-001), providing traceability from the test class to a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: Although performance/security testing is usually not applicable for unit tests, this method includes an explicit timeout (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which qualifies as an explicit performance-related assertion per the decision rules.

The test method name 'test8' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (methodName_scenario_expectedResult). Despite inline Given-When-Then comments, the method name fails the naming criteria.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are explicit indicators of auto-generated origins and generation artifacts: the EvoSuite test runner annotations, the class comment referencing auto-generated cases, and a generic test method name (test8). These are strong signals of heavy test generation rather than minimal hand-crafted tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given-When-Then comments and a descriptive class-level Javadoc; these indicate deliberate design intent. The use of a Category annotation also signals conscious test organization decisions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API methods (Grafo constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices) without accessing private fields or using reflection. No tight coupling to internals is evident.
Assertions use specific methods (assertEquals, assertNotSame) and include descriptive failure messages for key assertions, satisfying guidance to prefer specific assertions and include messages.
The method contains succinct Given-When-Then inline comments; the class has a focused Javadoc. Comments explain intent rather than restating obvious code and are not excessive.
No use of Random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies is present in the test method. The test logic is deterministic given the same environment.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test operates on local objects and does not persist data or modify global/static state in the method body. There is no file/database creation or missing cleanup visible in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level @Category(UnitTest.class) annotation is present, providing meaningful categorization for selective test execution.

PRINCIPLE: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior with a single Arrange-Act-Assert.
RATIONALE: Focused tests make root cause identification precise and avoid masking failures.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test tests exactly one behavior and has one clear Arrange-Act-Assert. Non-compliant if multiple distinct Act operations are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations. 2) Check test name for multiple operations. 3) If only one method call tested and one assertion group -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The method constructs a Grafo and asserts its numVertices() equals the constructor parameter. This is a single behavior (initial vertex count) with one clear Arrange (new Grafo), Act (numVertices()), Assert (assertEquals). No multiple unrelated operations are present.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests or execution order; use setup/teardown as needed.
RATIONALE: Independence enables flexible execution order and parallelism.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if uses @Before/@After or only local variables; non-compliant if shared mutable state is used without reset.
DECISION RULES: 1) Check for lifecycle annotations. 2) Check for shared mutable state. 3) If only local variables -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The test uses only local variables (grafo0, int0), no static/instance mutable state is used inside the method. No evidence of inter-test dependencies or ordered naming.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests must check both normal (happy path) and error/exceptional scenarios.
RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct handling of invalid inputs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if for each method under test there are at least two tests (happy and error) or explicit exception assertions; non-compliant if only happy paths are present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Count test methods and check for exception testing. 2) Look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows. 3) If class has <2 test methods and only happy path, non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The class has a single test method that tests only the happy path (constructing Grafo(2450) and asserting numVertices). There is no test for invalid inputs (e.g., negative size) or exception conditions.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate minimum, maximum, and off-by-one boundary values.
RATIONALE: Boundary conditions often harbor off-by-one and range errors.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests include empty, zero, negative, max values or names indicate boundary intent; non-compliant if only typical/middle-range values are used.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for data like 0, -1, Integer.MAX_VALUE, empty strings. 2) If only typical values present mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The test only uses a typical positive value (2450) and does not exercise boundaries like 0 or negative values.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and extract repeated setup into helpers or constants.
RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants used OR tests are very short and not duplicated; non-compliant if repeated code appears across tests.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for private helpers/constants. 2) If code appears in multiple tests mark non-compliant. 3) If tests are very short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code, mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The single test is short (<10 lines) and self-contained; there is no evidence of repeated code across multiple tests to refactor. Given only this single very small method, modularity concerns are minimal.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Keep test cases small and avoid loops/complex conditionals.
RATIONALE: Short, low-complexity tests are easier to understand and less error-prone.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test methods <20 lines and have no loops/complex conditionals.
DECISION RULES: 1) If any method >30 lines mark non-compliant. 2) If loops/complex conditionals present mark non-compliant. 3) If <15 lines and linear flow mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The method is short (~5 lines) and contains linear flow without loops or conditionals.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive, verifying multiple properties when applicable.
RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may pass even when behavior is incorrect; multiple checks increase fault detection.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions verify multiple properties (>=2) or collection size AND contents; non-compliant if only a single superficial assertion.
DECISION RULES: 1) If only 1 assertion (especially assertNotNull/assertTrue) mark non-compliant. 2) If >=2 property checks mark compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The test contains a single assertion (assertEquals(2450, int0)). While meaningful, it exercises only one property. No additional assertions verify related properties or side effects to increase fault detection.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or disabled tests; tests should be runnable and maintained.
RATIONALE: Ignored/disabled tests provide no value and hide regressions.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test code exists.
DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Ignore/@Disabled. 2) Search for commented-out @Test. 3) If none, mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The test is active (@Test present), there are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out test methods visible in the snippet.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be linked to requirements or tickets for traceability.
RATIONALE: Traceability helps map tests to requirements and eases impact analysis.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if annotations or Javadoc mention requirement IDs (REQ-, US-, JIRA-), or @Story/@Requirement present.
DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Story/@Requirement or requirement IDs in Javadoc. 2) If present, mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The class-level Javadoc explicitly references "REQ-GRAFO-001", providing traceability to a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate when relevant.
RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements are important and should be tested explicitly.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if explicit performance tests are present (e.g., @Test(timeout=...)) or security tests are included; otherwise not-applicable for many unit tests.
DECISION RULES: 1) Usually not-applicable for unit tests. 2) Mark compliant if @Test(timeout=...) or explicit performance/security checks are present.
VERDICT: compliant. The test method is annotated with @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint indicating a performance expectation for the test, satisfying the practice.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.
RATIONALE: Descriptive names are self-documenting and help identify failures quickly.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if method names follow descriptive patterns (e.g., methodName_condition_expected). Non-compliant if names are generic (test1, test7).
DECISION RULES: 1) Check naming patterns. 2) If generic names present mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The method name 'test7' is generic and does not communicate the scenario or expected result despite class-level Javadoc. A descriptive name like createGrafo_withSize_reportsSameNumVertices would be preferred.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing; avoid verbose auto-generated patterns.
RATIONALE: Verbose auto-generated tests are harder to maintain and often ignored.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Signs of heavy generation include auto-generated comments and names like test0, test1, test7.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for 'Auto-generated' comments or repetitive names. 2) If found with such patterns mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The presence of EvoSuite/EvoRunner imports and the generic method name 'test7' indicate the test shows signs of auto-generated code patterns. Although the file header mentions improvements, the method naming and test runner suggest generated origins.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show evidence of thoughtful design (Given-When-Then, BDD naming) and cover prioritized scenarios.
RATIONALE: Thoughtful design produces better coverage and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming present or multiple scenarios covered; non-compliant if tests appear minimal/basic.
DECISION RULES: 1) Search for Given-When-Then or BDD naming. 2) If only minimal happy-path test present mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. While the class Javadoc claims Given-When-Then improvements, the single method lacks explicit Given-When-Then structure and the test appears to be a single basic happy-path case without evidence of prioritized design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public API behavior and avoid coupling to internals.
RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle and easier to maintain.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests only call public methods and avoid reflection or accessing private internals.
DECISION RULES: 1) Check for reflection or private-field access. 2) If only public API calls are present mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The test only constructs a Grafo via its public constructor and calls the public numVertices() method. No reflection or private field access is present.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include descriptive failure messages where helpful.
RATIONALE: Descriptive assertions speed diagnosis and specific assertions catch subtle faults.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions include descriptive messages or use specific assert methods; non-compliant if assertions lack messages or use generic assertions unnecessarily.
DECISION RULES: 1) If >=50% of assertions have messages mark compliant. 2) If assertions use assertTrue when assertEquals is better mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant. The test uses assertEquals without a descriptive failure message. Because there is only one assertion and it lacks an explanatory message, the practice is not satisfied.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what; code should be self-explanatory.
RATIONALE: Useful comments help diagnose failures; excessive comments clutter the code.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if code is clean with minimal useful comments and no commented-out code; non-compliant if commented-out code or excessive comments exist.
DECISION RULES: 1) If commented-out code present mark non-compliant. 2) If >50% of lines are comments mark non-compliant. 3) Otherwise mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The class has concise Javadoc that documents requirement mapping, and no commented-out test code or excessive inline comments are present in the method snippet.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid randomness, time dependence, and external dependencies without mocking.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness and ensure reliable CI results.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), or external dependencies without mocks.
DECISION RULES: 1) If Random/System time/Thread.sleep found mark non-compliant. 2) If mocks used for non-deterministic sources mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The test uses deterministic code paths: constructor and numVertices() invocation. There are no calls to random/time APIs or sleeps, nor external dependencies visible in the snippet.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests must not modify shared state or leave side effects that affect other tests.
RATIONALE: Side-effect-free tests can run in any order and avoid inter-test interference.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables and have cleanup when external resources are used.
DECISION RULES: 1) If @After/@AfterEach cleanup present consider compliant. 2) If file/database/static modifications without cleanup mark non-compliant. 3) If local variables only mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The test uses only local variables and does not appear to persist data or modify shared/static state. No cleanup is necessary.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests for selective execution.
RATIONALE: Categorization enables running subsets (unit/integration/smoke) and managing CI resources.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category/@Category annotations are present and meaningful.
DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Tag/@Category. 2) If present and meaningful mark compliant.
VERDICT: compliant. The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) and defines the UnitTest interface, enabling categorization for selective execution.
